papers.abstract: As streaming video generation advances, enabling real-time interaction with generated video is becoming increasingly important. We introduce StreamEval, a unified benchmark for interactive streaming video generation spanning five tasks: avatar dialogue, avatar performance, world generation, instruction editing, and reference editing. StreamEval comprises 300 scripted test cases lasting 15-300s, each specifying initial assets, incrementally arriving multimodal requests, and explicit requirements for state changes and content preservation. Performance is assessed along four evaluation dimensions: task execution, state consistency, visual fidelity, and audiovisual coordination, instantiated through ten task-specific metrics on a 0-100 scale. Evaluating 37 distinct models across 300 test cases, we find that high visual quality and identity retention do not necessarily coincide with reliable request execution or sustained state consistency. In particular, request execution remains challenging: the highest task-specific scores are 36.90 for Following among seven avatar-performance models, 25.93 for Following in text-conditioned world generation, and 15.00 for Edit Success among three reported reference-editing models. These findings identify reliable request execution under timing and preservation constraints as a central challenge for advancing omni-modal real-time interactive systems. The leaderboard is available at https://streameval.ai

papers.abstract: Spatial intelligence requires agents to actively acquire visual evidence and integrate observations into a coherent representation of the three-dimensional world. Yet spatial question answering offers limited evidence of whether models can construct accurate metric maps through autonomous exploration. We introduce SpatialScout, a benchmark for evaluating vision-language model (VLM) agents on active object-level 3D mapping. SpatialScout comprises 80 diverse indoor scenes containing 3,140 target objects. Given an object inventory, RGB observations, camera calibration, and camera poses, agents control a camera to explore each scene and estimate object centers in a shared coordinate frame. The task requires coordinating viewpoint selection, cross-view association, geometric estimation, and map revision under bounded interaction budgets. Evaluation jointly measures localization accuracy and target coverage through object-scale overlap scores that penalize missing predictions. Experiments with frontier VLMs reveal substantial limitations: the strongest evaluated model, Claude Opus 5.5, achieves a mean overlap score of 41.71%, with 47.23% of targets exceeding an intersection-over-union (IoU) threshold of 0.5 and only 3.25% exceeding 0.9. These results reveal a substantial gap between recovering coarse object layouts and constructing complete, precise metric maps. SpatialScout provides a quantitative testbed for developing agents that build reliable 3D spatial representations through active perception. Code is available at https://github.com/JesseZZZZZ/SpatialScout.
takeaways: The object is a benchmark for active 3D mapping, not a new model architecture.
The visible limit is the substantial gap between coarse layout recovery and precise metric map construction.

papers.abstract: Despite recent progress in dexterous reference tracking, existing models focus primarily on single-hand manipulation and a limited range of interactions, leaving the bimanual dexterous behaviors common in real life unaddressed. The scarcity of contact-rich bimanual manipulation data and the increased complexity of coordinating contacts make developing a generalist bimanual tracker particularly challenging. Therefore, we present 1) DONIC, the first generalist bimanual tracker jointly trained across operation categories and human-motion sources, together with 2) BiHOI, a multi-view dataset of 1,575 sequences spanning 229 objects and emphasizing sustained bimanual interaction, where reconstructed interactions are retargeted into robot references. DONIC combines proximal policy optimization with behavioral cloning in a feedback loop that recycles verified successful executions into training demonstrations. An object-centered per-hand reward maintains object-motion feedback while supervising each hand according to its reference contact role. Clip-Centered Advantages remove reference-dependent advantage offsets while preserving within-trajectory differences. Together, these designs enable one single policy to learn coordinated manipulation across heterogeneous references. Without finetuning, a single checkpoint achieves 86.79% success on unseen trajectories of training objects and 57.32% on held-out objects, surpassing the state-of-the-art bimanual tracking baselines by 77.36 and 45.73 percentage points.

papers.abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) agents can handle increasingly complex tasks, navigating long trajectories of observations and actions. As these trajectories grow, key-value (KV) cache I/O and storage become the dominant cost. Trajectories can also exceed the LLM's maximum context length, requiring control over active cache growth. Prior work uses context engineering to reduce cache size by trimming or summarizing history. However, modifying the trajectory prefix invalidates subsequent cached states and triggers costly re-prefilling of retained context. Task accuracy can also suffer when too little context is retained to limit re-prefill costs. We propose cache engineering as a new scheme. It allows agents to directly control their active KV cache without modifying the trajectory or re-prefilling retained context. Specifically, agents can proactively use drop to exclude selected cache from future attention and repos to adjust retained keys' position encodings. We formalize these cache operations and identify history dependence as a serving challenge: identical token sequences can yield different cache states under different cache operation sequences, making prefix matching insufficient for correct cache reuse. Thus, we co-design the AKV serving engine. It provides a stateless interface compatible with existing serving APIs, while internally managing stateful cache reuse, eviction, and restoration. Experiments show that a tool-response rolling-drop cache policy improves average benchmark scores by 1.7 points and reduces average cost by 27.7%, compared with conventional threshold-triggered summarization. With AKV, it achieves up to 1.2x the output throughput and a 1.5x speedup in P95 request latency. Recursive self-improvement of cache policies further reduces cost by 7.1% over expert design. Our code is at https://github.com/thu-nics/AKV.
takeaways: The core object is a serving engine and cache operation scheme that decouples cache state management from trajectory modification.
A visible limit is that identical token sequences can yield different cache states under different operation sequences, complicating standard prefix matching.

papers.abstract: For a centered homogeneous generalized Gaussian field with spectral weight $C|\omega|^{-\gamma}$, we prove two-endpoint recovery of normalized posterior wavelet covariances under fixed finite admissible observations. Global dilation symmetry holds if and only if all observation functions vanish. The nonzero wavelet and the observation functions are real Schwartz functions with $M\geq1$ vanishing moments, with $C>0$ and $\gamma<2M+1$. Noise is Gaussian and field-independent, and total observation covariance is positive definite. Under simultaneous dilation of target scales and positions, multiplication by $\lambda^{-\gamma}$ recovers the prior covariance as $\lambda\downarrow0$ and $\lambda\uparrow\infty$, uniformly on every fixed compact target set. If a nonzero observation function exists, additional finite first nonzero Fourier orders $m_\psi,m_i$ at zero of the wavelet and nonzero observation functions yield compact-uniform recovery bounds $O(\lambda^{2m_\psi+1-\gamma})$ and $O(\lambda^{-(2\min_i m_i+1-\gamma)})$, with leading coefficients and cancellation-dependent improvements. The bounds are exact leading orders when their coefficients are nonzero. For the Mat\'ern-type spectrum $S(\omega)=C(\kappa^2+\omega^2)^{-p}$, $\kappa>0$, $1/2<p<M+1/2$, fixed finite noisy point observations yield distinct compact-uniform limits: the homogeneous $C|\omega|^{-2p}$ kernel after multiplication by $\lambda^{-2p}$ at small scales, and the constant-spectrum $S(0)$ kernel without normalization at large scales. A projection-norm criterion treats fixed closed observation subspaces; Mexican-hat formulas illustrate the finite-observation results.

A visible limit is that global dilation symmetry holds only if all observation functions vanish, restricting the symmetry conditions.

papers.abstract: Separately amplifying gate, latency, and mid-circuit measurement errors can simplify zero-noise extrapolation, but a weak interaction between amplification knobs does not establish an accurate zero-noise limit. We distinguish observable separability, response-model adequacy, and calibration of that limit, and test them in a pre-specified $2^3$ factorial experiment on three IBM dynamic circuits. For the primary echoed spectator observable, the latency-measurement coefficient is $b_{LM}=+0.0007$ with a nominal 95% bootstrap interval $[-0.0033,+0.0049]$. A separately planned follow-up meets a $\pm0.005$ equivalence criterion and recovers two injected interactions; both repeat runs nevertheless trigger the drift rule. Multi-knob extrapolations have smaller median absolute errors than the single-knob comparisons, yet all five original strategies exclude the known ideal value for three of six observables. Duration controls support a model-dependent contribution to the spectator deficit from unequal decay rates in native padding and added delay. We give an explicit construction showing why measurements at two measurement-knob levels cannot identify the extrapolated limit without response assumptions. A post-hoc precision analysis and an additive full-factorial estimator expose a further bias-variance trade-off hidden by point-error comparisons. The experiment provides a diagnostic of the implemented response surface, not a certification of physical channel independence or mitigation accuracy.

papers.abstract: Software supply chain attacks continue to be on the rise, exploiting the trust that helps open source ecosystems thrive. Recent incidents like the Shai-Hulud worm and the Axios compromise demonstrate that a single malicious package can have wide reaching and devastating impacts overnight. These high profile attacks can be traced back to the same culprit: package registries. Although they are a useful convenience to pull prebuilt packages from, is such a commonly exploited component of the software supply chain worth the risk? In this paper, we investigate whether removing the registry from the developer workflow by building packages directly from source can serve as a malware prevention strategy - effectively removing an entire attack surface. Our hypothesis is that malicious packages avoid attributing a source to minimize visibility, while benign packages seek exposure and therefore link to their repositories. We evaluate this through three research questions: how effective is building from source at avoiding malware, how feasible is it to build from source in the current state of the supply chain, and how the building from source strategy compares to state-of-the-art security scanners. To do so, we (1) construct an aggregate dataset of 47,066 malicious packages from four academic and one industry malicious datasets source across npm and PyPI ecosystems, (2) build a snapshot index of all 3.9 million npm and 764 thousand PyPI packages, and (3) analyze all malicious samples alongside a statistically significant sample of 16,569 packages from each registry, totaling 33,138 packages. We find that simply checking for a source has a success rate between 87.7 and 99.9 percent of preventing malware, depending on the level of source vetting. Consequently, there is a significant lack of transparency within benign packages, with only 47.4 percent attributing a source an end user could build from.

papers.abstract: We investigate phase-coherent multistatic sensing in distributed ISAC systems where spatially separated access points (APs) share a common, non-ideal local oscillator (LO) impaired by phase noise (PN). papers.abstract: Public procurement laws trade rules against discretion with value thresholds: below them, buyers use faster and less competitive procedures. Colombia offers an unusually clean setting to measure how much buyers manipulate estimated values to stay below the line and what it costs. Thresholds are entity-specific (five budget bands set by law) and move every January with the minimum wage, while the round numbers that usually confound bunching estimates stay fixed. Using the universe of Colombian procurement records (SECOP I and II, 2011-2026; 8,569,218 SECOP II processes) and each entity-year's own threshold, we find sharp bunching of estimated values just below both legal cutoffs: 49,631 excess processes below the small-purchase threshold (86% of the mass observed in the last five percent below it) and 3,157 below the tender threshold. The spike tracks the threshold, not the round numbers: it moves with the minimum wage, appears only at each entity's own band, and is an order of magnitude smaller for procedures that carry no value cap. Territorial governments, run by elected mayors and governors, bunch more than appointed national agencies at the small-purchase threshold, even after reweighting for budget band, object and year. Processes bunched below the tender threshold attract half as many bidders as those just above it, obtain smaller discounts, and are more often enlarged after award. A second source of variation, the four-month ban on direct contracting before presidential elections, shows that buyers respond to rules on the timing margin: direct contracting falls by 95% during the ban and rises by 209% in the two weeks before it, in each of four electoral cycles, with a partial shift toward below-threshold procedures. Chile's fixed UTM thresholds display the same pattern, and a cutoff abolished in 2024 shows no bunching afterwards.

papers.abstract: The basic reproduction number, $R_0$, is central to infectious-disease modelling, yet analytic expressions can be difficult to derive for high-dimensional, nonlinear, or structurally complex models. We introduce REEBLRA ($R_0$ Equation Estimation using Bayesian Logistic Regression Algorithm), an interpretable framework that learns explicit surrogate equations for epidemic thresholds from parameter--response data. Rather than directly regressing $R_0$, REEBLRA estimates $\Pr\{R_0(\boldsymbol\theta)>c\}$ for parameter vector $\boldsymbol\theta$ and threshold $c$. It provides a binary equation for classifying epidemic invasion ($R_0>1$) and successive threshold equations defining ordered brackets that approximate $R_0$, the expected number of secondary infections caused by a typical case in a fully susceptible population. The resulting equations support parameter screening, sensitivity interpretation, threshold classification, and exploratory analysis when analytic derivation is cumbersome. Bayesian logistic regression using standardized polynomial-like features and proper weakly informative priors yields regularized estimates, posterior uncertainty, and finite coefficients under complete or quasi-complete separation. We establish a mechanistic--surrogate concordance principle linking the full fitted-score gradient to the local gradient of $\log R_0$ under explicit regularity and tangency assumptions, allowing conditional interpretation of threshold directions. Across seven analytic-label benchmarks associated with ODE models, including a 15-compartment five-group SIR system, five-fold binary AUC was 0.999--1.000 and ordered-bracket accuracy was 0.951--0.998. REEBLRA complements rather than replaces mechanistic derivations, bridging simulation, machine learning, and reproduction-number analysis. An accompanying Shiny app supports implementation.
takeaways: The object is a Bayesian logistic regression framework that produces explicit surrogate equations for epidemic thresholds rather than direct regression of the reproduction number.
